elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that Customer is not liable for any liquidated damages in respect of late payment and replaces the original liquidated-damages obligation with simple interest.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that Customer is not liable for any penalty or similar charge in respect of late payment.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer may arise only as an early-termination fee triggered by early termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no liquidated amount on Customer at all; accordingly, there is no liquidated amount arising outside an early-termination fee.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed by the rendered clause, so no fee exceeds the three-month cap.

elements.element: An early-termination fee must be the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no liquidated amount and expressly eliminates the original late-payment liquidated damages.

result.reason: The redline reaches the preferred position by eliminating the late-payment liquidated damages and penalties; complete elimination also complies with the less protective fallback. It is not minimal because it additionally introduces a proper-and-undisputed-invoice condition, makes interest Vendor's sole remedy, and adds a Section 7.3 withholding rule. The drafting is materially problematic because 'Vendor's sole remedy' may unintentionally bar other contractual or legal remedies for nonpayment, and the clause does not state whether interest on amounts ultimately found due accrues retroactively from the original due date or only from that determination.
